fixes.explanation: Judge is the word, friend. Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), says let no one judge you by what you eat or drink. He even adds a feast, a New Moon or a Sabbath to the list. So when somebody squints at your plate, you may keep right on chewing.

Praise sounds so much nicer, friend, but it's not the word in this verse. Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), says let no one judge you by what you eat or drink. Nobody is handing out gold stars for your lunch here. It's about people sizing you up over food and drink, and he says don't let them.

Reward would be a sweet deal, a cookie for every meal, but that's not what the verse says. Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), says let no one judge you by what you eat or drink. The word is judge. Nobody gets to hold a scorecard over your plate.

True! Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), puts a Sabbath on the list right beside a feast and a New Moon. His words are, “Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.” That's a whole list, friend, and not one seat on it for a scorekeeper.

This one is true, friend, and the Sabbath is right there in the verse. Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), says, “Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.” It sits in a list with a feast and a New Moon. Easy to blink and miss when the list is that long.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, so I get why it jumped out. But Paul says “…the body that casts it belongs to Christ.” The shadow is food, drink, feasts, New Moons and Sabbaths, and the body behind it is Christ's. Keep your eyes on the One casting it, friend.

Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), is a good guess. But that's not who Paul names here. He says the shadow is cast by a body, and “…the body that casts it belongs to Christ.” Good name, friend, but Paul points to Someone else.
Paul wrote the letter (Colossians 1:1), so I see why he came to mind. But he doesn't take the job for himself. He says the body “…grows as God causes it to grow.” I think that's a humble man, friend.
Perish! Paul says, “These will all perish with use…” Then he gives the reason: “…because they are based on human commands and teachings.” That's straight from the verse, friend.
Multiply is what dough does on my apron, friend, but not what Paul says here. He says, “These will all perish with use…” Perishing is the word, not multiplying.
Things that get better the more you use them would be nice, friend. But Paul says, “These will all perish with use…” Improving isn't in the verse. Perishing is.
